correctness.rationale: For n=2^a p q the deficiency is pq-(2^(a+1)-1)(p+q+1). Positivity forces p>2^(a+1)-1; reduction modulo q then excludes q from the deficient divisor. Squarefreeness of the odd part leaves exactly the cases d=2^e and d=2^e p, and each gives one explicit divisor parametrization whose converse is verified by substitution. Edge cases and an independent bounded exact-integer cross-check were also verified.

originality.rationale: The 2013 foundational paper's stated two-prime classification, the 2014 primary paper ruling out odd three-prime deficient-perfect numbers, current OEIS A271816 including its 2026 updates, the 2019 deficient-perfect paper, synonymous formula searches, and the current SCOPE archive were checked. No located source states the exact two-family classification for 2^a p q or an equivalent fixed-a divisor parametrization. Originality remains to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk from older terminology and incomplete direct access to the full 2013 article.

value.rationale: The theorem closes a natural first even three-prime slice beyond the known two-prime classification and the impossibility of the odd three-prime case. It replaces an open-ended prime search by finitely many divisor tests for each a, proves the larger odd prime can never divide the deficiency, and yields explicit prime bounds while reproducing the known initial sequence values.
